page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16ms_v2 is a constrained-core, memory-dense virtual machine within the FXms_v2 family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores at a 4.2 GHz clock frequency. It incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an extensive 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The hardware allocation pairs these 16 vCPUs with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an unusually high ratio of 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring remote network storage configurations, and no discrete GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded compute throughput alongside solid memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core performance (2,336.0) and text processing (2,948.0), bolstered by 4.2 GHz base frequencies. Single-threaded data compression and decompression routines rank in the upper quartile, showing 34.66 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.31 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded metrics register in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,705.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 29,487.26, reflecting the capped 16-vCPU topology. Memory throughput reaches 131.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 90.97 GB/sec for writes.

The constrained-core design presents distinct cost efficiencies for software licensed on a per-core basis, such as relational database engines and proprietary electronic design automation (EDA) tooling. By limiting active execution threads while delivering 672.0 GB of RAM and high single-core clocks, workloads avoid unnecessary core license fees without sacrificing memory capacity. The primary hardware tradeoff is the total lack of ephemeral local NVMe storage and absence of accelerator hardware.

The FX32-16ms_v2 is architecturally aligned with memory-intensive workloads that require rapid per-core processing rather than broad parallel scaling. Prime operational targets include in-memory databases, SAP HANA, memory-bound analytics pipelines, large-footprint EDA simulations, and per-core licensed enterprise platforms.
